description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) while measuring the critical-infrastructure
milestone (#1607).  Found from Moo's own suite, where every file that uses
Test::Fatal's `exception { â¦ }` stops at the first call.

WHAT HAPPENS.  `Pl/ExprToCL.pm` keeps `%RUNTIME_NAMES` (line ~145): "Runtime
built-in names (from pcl-runtime.lisp export list, p- prefix stripped).  These
get the p- prefix in generated code; user-defined subs get pl-."  The table is
consulted at the CALL SITE and it does NOT ask whether the program has DECLARED
a sub of that name â so a declaration and its calls disagree.  The sub is
emitted correctly as `pl-NAME`; every call to it goes to `p-NAME`.

TWO REPRODUCERS, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl
(scratch/s481b/probe-name-collision.pl, probe-collide-hash.pl):

  (a) LOUD â the runtime symbol is not a function:

      sub exception { return "MINE(@_)" }
      print exception("a"), "\n";

      perl: MINE(a)
      PCL : The function pcl:p-exception is undefined.
            (`p-exception` is a DEFINE-CONDITION, not a defun)

  (b) SILENT WRONG â the runtime symbol IS a function:

      sub hash { return "MINEHASH" }
      print hash(), "\n";

      perl: MINEHASH
      PCL : (an empty line â `(p-hash)` built an empty anonymous hash)

The emission for (b) shows both halves:

      (p-sub pl-hash (&rest %_args) â¦ (p-tail-value "MINEHASH"))
      â¦
      (p-print (p-list-ctx (p-hash)) (p-esc "\n"))

THE POPULATION, measured (scratch/s481b/collision-scan.pl reads the qw() block
and filters to identifiers that are not perl builtins): **347 entries, 201
legal Perl sub names, 34 of them NOT perl builtins** â

    and aref aslice backslash backtick box break can continue cwd decf
    defined defpackage exception flatten gethash hash hslice incf isa let
    not or reftype regex set_up_inc setf subst typeglob (+ the rest listed
    by the script)

Names a real distribution defines: `exception` (Test::Fatal), `can` / `isa`
(every hand-written UNIVERSAL override), `reftype`, `cwd`, `regex`, `hash`,
`box`, `flatten`.  A perl BUILTIN in the table is not at risk in the same way â
perl itself would not call a user sub of that name without `&` â so the
non-builtin subset is the bug's population.

FIX SHAPE (not done here; this was a measurement batch).  The call site already
knows the program's declared subs (`Pl::Environment`'s `declared_subs`, the
same table `_bareword_callable_here` reads, keyed by BARE name since #413).
A DECLARED sub must win over `%RUNTIME_NAMES` for every entry that is not a
perl builtin; for a perl builtin the existing precedence is right and must not
move.  Rule 11 applies: `Pl::ExprToCL::is_runtime_name` is the ONE read of this
table and the fix belongs there, not beside it.

BAR: a `Pl/t` guard with one row per non-builtin name at risk (define a sub of
that name, call it, compare with perl), plus a NEGATIVE row proving a perl
builtin still routes to the runtime.  Emission changes, so corpus-diff +
emission-ab + a generation bump; the sweep per the WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN table.

=== RESIDUE MEASURED (s536a, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) -- the UNDECLARED half: a sub installed at RUN time under a runtime-internal name ===
#2100 made a DECLARED (or imported) sub of such a name win at the call site (`_name_is_declared_sub`).  A sub installed by a COMPUTED glob write is not declared anywhere the compiler can see, so its plain call still lowers to the runtime operator.  Test::Deep builds its constructors in a loop -- `my $sub = sub { require $file; $full_pkg->new(@_) }; *{$name} = $sub;` for Hash, Array, ... -- and Test::Deep::wrap calls `hash($data)`: emitted `(p-hash $data)` (the runtime's anonymous-hash constructor), while `array($data)` is `(|Test::Deep|::pl-array ...)` because `array` is not in %RUNTIME_NAMES.  wrap() then answers an UNBLESSED hash and `$d2->descend($d1)` dies "Can't locate object method "descend" via package "main"" on the second cmp_deeply of a hash.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s536a/p/4104-2.pl):
    use Test::More; use Test::Deep qw/ cmp_deeply /;
    my $e2 = { pi => 1 };
    my $w = Test::Deep::wrap($e2); print "# wrap e2: ", ref($w), "\n";
    cmp_deeply({ pi => 1 }, $e2, "h1"); done_testing;
  perl 5.40.3: `# wrap e2: Test::Deep::Hash` / ok 1.   PCL (06a4b8ba): `# wrap e2: ` / dies.
  Reduced in plain perl: `BEGIN { *{"main::hash"} = sub { "MINE" } } print hash(1), "\n";` -- perl `MINE` (`hash` is no perl builtin), PCL `1` (the runtime operator ran).

perl's rule: a non-keyword bareword followed by `(` is ALWAYS a sub call, declared or not; %RUNTIME_NAMES entries that are NOT perl keywords (hash flatten box setf let regex aslice gethash ...) can only be hijacks at a SOURCE call.  FIX SHAPE (not built here -- a compiler change wider than the batch): in cl_name's runtime-name branch, a for_funcall SOURCE word that is not `is_core_keyword` lowers to `pl-NAME` whether declared or not; first measure whether any compiler path synthesises a funcall node with such a name (corpus-diff + the wide emission-ab name the sites).
ROWS: YAML-PP-v0.39.0-0 54.glob.t *PLAN* and 37.schema-perl.t *PLAN* (re-keyed from #4104 by s536a).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a user sub whose NAME is in `%RUNTIME_NAMES` is hijacked at the CALL SITE â `sub hash {â¦}; hash()` calls PCL's `p-hash` and prints nothing; `sub exception {â¦}; exception("a")` dies "The function pcl:p-exception is undefined".  34 of the table's entries are legal Perl sub names that are NOT perl builtins (exception, hash, can, isa, reftype, cwd, regex, box, break, continue, let, flatten, â¦).  Test::Fatal's `exception` is one, so it costs Moo test files.
